comment: F4-06 default-DENY seccomp profile for the portfolio-terminal service.
Every syscall the container may make is an explicit ALLOW below, each with a
one-line justification. Everything not listed returns EPERM (SCMP_ACT_ERRNO).
Methodology (empirical, 2026-10-09): syscalls were collected via strace -f -qc
inside a debian:trixie-slim sandbox while driving, per demo (minishell, ft-ls,
ft-select, ft-linear-regression): an interactive login bash on a pty (mirroring
the service's pexpect spawn), `make` (full gcc/ld pipeline), and the built demo
binary; plus a full trace of the service itself (python/uvicorn/pexpect/boto3)
running one real WS session end-to-end. Union of traces = the base allow list;
near-certain needs of paths not exercised in the traces (ASAN shadow mapping,
bash builtins, timer syscalls) are added and marked [expected] in the why.
Verification: live-verified 2026-10-11 (dev compose stack mounts this file
in docker-compose.dev.yml): all four demos compile and run under it through
the real proxy chain (mint token -> WS -> make -> run -> post-session sweep),
and a denied-syscall probe (unshare/ptrace/bpf/kcmp) returns EPERM without
SIGSYS. Two gaps the original traces missed were found and fixed empirically:
fchdir (coreutils rm -rf safe directory walking) and the utimensat family
(touch / gcc -o timestamps). Transcripts:
.github/agent-reports/senior-dev/f4-06-seccomp-default-deny.md. Drift guard:
tests/security/test_seccomp_profile.py pins the structure (default DENY,
allow-list only, documented entries).
EXPLICITLY DENIED (by omission, default EPERM): unshare, setns, mount, umount2,
pivot_root, chroot, ptrace, process_vm_(read|write)v, bpf, keyctl, add_key,
request_key, kexec_*, reboot, (f)init_module/delete_module, iopl, ioperm,
swapon/swapoff, sethostname/setdomainname, capset, perf_event_open,
userfaultfd, io_uring_setup, open_by_handle_at, fanotify_init, quotactl,
kcmp, uselib, vhangup, clock_settime/settimeofday (time tampering),
personality (ABI bypass), setuid/setgid family (privilege change),
sched_setscheduler (scheduler control), memfd_secret, landlock_* .
This is the structural improvement over the pre-F4-06 profile (default-ALLOW
with ~24 deny entries): an unknown or dangerous syscall now fails CLOSED by
construction — the old deny list cannot drift out of date.

syscalls.why: File I/O core: fchdir for safe directory walking (rm -rf/coreutils openat-safer), bash builtins (ls/cat/cd/pwd), gcc+ld reading sources and writing .o/binary, make's directory scans, the service unzipping demo files, pty ioctls (TIOCGWINSZ winsize, termios), ft_ls's stat family. utimensat/futimesat/utime(s): timestamp updates on own files (touch, coreutils temp-file bookkeeping, gcc -o rewrite; futimens is a glibc wrapper over utimensat) — DAC limits these to files the session owns. statx: the container RUNTIME (runc) itself calls statx(STATX_MNT_ID) during container setup — without it no process starts. ioctl stays unfiltered: the pty/winsize/termios paths need varied constants; an args filter breaks legitimate termios values.

Memory management: dynamic loaders, malloc arenas (brk companion), ASAN shadow reservation for the ft_linear_regression build (-fsanitize=address reserves ~14TB of PROT_NONE shadow — must mmap), pty buffers. mlock/munlock: [expected] sanitizer/runtime pinning paths.
Heap growth for bash, gcc, and demo binaries (observed in every trace).

Signal plumbing: bash job control (SIGINT/SIGQUIT handlers), make pipeline signals, pexpect's Ctrl+C forwarding (kill), glibc raise()/pthread_kill (tgkill). sigaltstack: ASAN installs its own alternate signal stack at startup — without it the ft_linear_regression demo (built -fsanitize=address) aborts with 'CHECK failed ... sigaltstack' (empirically proven under this profile). Legacy signal(2)/sigaction(2) aliases kept for non-glibc demo code paths.
Process lifecycle: every exec terminates through exit_group; bash reaps jobs and the service reaps the pty child via wait4 (pexpect close). waitpid is the legacy alias.

Process creation: bash forks every external command, make forks gcc, python's asyncio executor threads use clone(2) (clone+clone3 in the service trace); vfork is bash's optimization for simple commands (observed). clone is NOT args-filtered to block CLONE_NEW* — libseccomp flag filtering breaks glibc posix_spawn paths; namespace escape is instead denied by this profile refusing unshare/setns AND by the boot self-check probing unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER).

Executing bash itself, every command typed in the demo shell (ls, make, gcc, ./binary), and python child processes. WHAT is exec'd is restricted by the command VALIDATOR (line-accumulating, deny-first allowlist); seccomp is the layer below, not a duplicate of it.

glibc/runtime thread setup — every modern ELF (bash, gcc, python) runs arch_prctl(ARCH_SET_FS) + set_tid_address + set_robust_list + rseq at startup (all four in every trace). prlimit64/setrlimit: the service's OWN preexec_fn sets per-session rlimits between fork and exec; getrlimit: bash's ulimit builtin. prctl: glibc/pty setup (in the service trace).
Thread synchronization: python GIL/asyncio (observed in the service trace), gcc/ld link sections. futex_time64: [expected] 32-bit-time fallback path.

Process identity + job control: bash computes its prompt, job control calls setpgid per pipeline and setsid when it must detach (both observed in interactive traces); python uses gettid for logging. Identity syscalls return kernel truth about the caller only — no capability granted.

Credential READS (get*): bash, make, python query them constantly (observed). setgroups/setgid/setuid/setfsuid/setfsgid/setres*: the container RUNTIME (runc) drops to the container user via setgroups+setgid+setuid during setup — without them no process starts (empirically: container aborts in libcontainer setupUser) — and bash's own job-control probes call them; all are no-ops privilege-wise for the non-root coder user (uid 1000 — setting your own uid/gid, raising is impossible without a setuid binary, which the image has none of). No privilege is reachable: container runs non-root with cap_drop ALL.

Time + entropy: python time.monotonic (session idle/lifetime timers), asyncio scheduling, bash prompt timing, getrandom for dict hashing / gcc temp names / ASLR canaries (observed in every trace), nanosleep for the read-pump pacing. Write-side time syscalls (clock_settime, settimeofday) stay DENIED by omission.
Event multiplexing: uvicorn's epoll loop (epoll_* in the service trace), bash/readline pselect6 for interactive input (observed), make's poll, signalfd4 from pty/script interactions (observed).

Sockets REQUIRED despite no raw-socket demos: (a) the service is a network server — uvicorn binds :8000 and accepts WS connections (bind/accept in the service trace); (b) outbound sync — demo-whitelist feed and R2 downloads use HTTPS, and glibc NSS (getaddrinfo, /etc/nsswitch) itself socket()s (connect observed in ALL traces); (c) pty pair allocation via socketpair (observed); (d) bash's own connect: NSS/group lookups. Network EGRESS is contained by the deploy environment (Render private network / compose network), NOT seccomp — documented in the platform decision note (D9).

The container RUNTIME (runc) applies the capability bounding set via capset during container setup — without it no process starts (empirically: 'unable to apply caps: operation not permitted' aborts the container). capget: glibc capability queries during exec. Inside the container this grants nothing: the bounding set is empty (cap_drop ALL) and the user is non-root.
Scheduler queries + yield: python cpu_count (sched_getaffinity in the service trace), gcc yield under contention. sched_setscheduler stays DENIED by omission.
getrusage: bash's `time` builtin and make's child accounting (observed). getcpu: [expected] NUMA-aware allocator paths.
membarrier: glibc malloc/rseq synchronization on modern kernels ([expected] python 3.14 runtime). get/set_mempolicy + mbind: [expected] NUMA policy queries; harmless no-ops on non-NUMA hosts.
Durability: gcc writing objects, the manifest tmp+rename pattern, bash flushing (fdatasync observed in interactive traces).
Scatter-gather I/O: python buffered WS-frame writes ([expected] uvicorn path), gcc object writes — standard glibc stdio path under load.
asyncio event-loop primitives ([expected]: uvicorn wakeup fds; timerfd for the health-check and whitelist-sync cadence).

ft_ls links -lacl and reads POSIX ACL xattrs (lgetxattr/llistxattr observed in the ft-ls trace); coreutils ls strips the ACL '+' marker via the same calls. Writes/removals included so the demo behaves exactly like a real ls on ACL-bearing files.
